## R4 admitted-frame delivery and pre-ACK retirement assurance (2026-10-30)

**Authoring parent:** `b76f62917479ff3a1e512d7c6c791157d97d2f2c`. The first-round R4 audit traced the current
production route from a current R2 lease and `GraphicsReady` through joined
`drdynvc`, RDPGFX CAPS/CREATE, exact CREATE_SURFACE/MAP_SURFACE_TO_OUTPUT
accepted-byte receipts, synchronous native framebuffer borrow, ClearCodec
preparation, bounded DATA_FIRST/DATA publication and R4 ACK membership. R2 is
revalidated before every graphics write slice, when accepted bytes are committed
into R3, before client Graphics DATA intake and before/after ACK consumption.
Only the last fully accepted frame record calls R4
`completeFrameDelivery(..., deliveredWireBytes)`; zero progress, deferred
credit, conclusively unwritten cancellation and partial publication do not create
ACK membership.

**Uncovered assurance boundary:** existing tests separately covered complete
DATA -> ACK, pending DATA -> Share/DVC loss, and isolated R4 delivered-credit ->
generation retirement, but did not exercise the production R3 DVC order
**fully delivered frame -> one R4 ACK credit -> session/DVC retirement -> late
FRAME_ACK**. Add ordinary production-backed CTest
`graphics.frame-delivery-session-retirement-before-ack` using the existing
`test_owned_mcs_connect_initial` executable. It fully accepts every outer
frame record, proves one outstanding R4 frame, invokes the same DVC
`close()` reached by `McsSessionLifecycle::close()` and R2 session
retirement, then proves a late ACK returns `Closed` with zero outstanding
credit and no buffered Graphics DATA. This is a test-only assurance increment:
**no production source, codec, frame scheduling or ACK policy changes**.

**Agent 10 frame-acceptance contract:** a frame is eligible only while the exact
R2 lease is current, MCS/PersonalDesktop Share is activated, the advertised
Client Core 0x0100 RDPGFX capability is present, the joined `drdynvc` route
owns a current DVC generation, RDPGFX VERSION8/VERSION81 negotiation is
confirmed, and CREATE_SURFACE plus MAP_SURFACE_TO_OUTPUT have completed for the
current geometry. Native geometry/capture generation must still match at the
synchronous borrow. R3 may report frame publication complete only after every
outer TLS plaintext slice is positively accepted and the mapped frame payload
equals the prepared owned wire extent; only then may R4 add the exact frame ID
to its bounded 64-entry ACK window. Resize must drain or explicitly suspend old
ACK membership before DELETE/CREATE/MAP; same-DVC remap fences retired frame
IDs. Share/R2/native-owner retirement closes R3/R4 before later ACK callbacks.
A genuine first-frame acceptance claim requires both the exact frame write
receipt and a matching current-generation FRAME_ACK; the former alone is not
client-visible presentation evidence.

**Future owner-private physical checklist:** on one R9-approved exact SHA and
only after separate owner authorization, record the admitted connection/session
generation, verified R2 native lease, Share activation and joined `drdynvc`;
Client Core 0x0100 and selected RDPGFX VERSION8/VERSION81; exact CREATE/MAP
receipts and mapped geometry; native capture generation/stride/extent; first
ClearCodec frame ID and total prepared wire bytes; every positive R1 accepted
slice through the final DATA record; R4 outstanding credit changing 0 -> 1;
matching client FRAME_ACK changing 1 -> 0; resize DELETE/CREATE/MAP and first
post-remap frame/ACK; then Stop/lock/logout/session replacement and reconnect
with a fresh R2/DVC generation and no stale ACK effect. Stop at the first
missing boundary and mark later stages NOT REACHED. Do not record pixels,
credentials or other private identifiers.

## R1 Round 2 continuation — realistic delegated final-authInfo TLS framing (2026-10-30)

**Authoring parent:** `1371b43d1b8c0e2a88d044894c932c9ad611e6e1`. R2/R6 current executable evidence is not an R1 failure: the Microsoft SSPI oracle still omits `ISC_REQ_DELEGATE`, so its final authInfo delegates empty username/password fields. Agent 6 owns that request-flag correction and exact Windows rerun. R1 therefore does not change TLS versions, certificates, Type-2 bytes, socket polling, timeouts or retry policy.

**R1 coverage audit:** the existing production-backed `runtime.linux-direct-ntlm-final-authinfo-tls-fragments-reconnect` already uses valid nonempty `TSPasswordCreds`, but its small `rdp` / `Password` final authInfo is written as only 1/2/3/remainder bytes. It does not cross the `TsRequestFrameReader` 512-byte TLS-read scratch boundary, isolate body/final-byte fragmentation, or prove that application plaintext coalesced immediately after a complete final TSRequest remains outside the CredSSP owner. That is a test-coverage gap, not a demonstrated production transport defect.

This increment adds no production code. New behavior CTest `runtime.linux-direct-ntlm-final-authinfo-large-fragments-coalesced-tail-reconnect` reuses the existing real listener/TLS/Direct-NTLM lifecycle executable with a bounded valid 32-code-unit username and 192-code-unit password. Its protected final authInfo is 518 bytes, uses canonical outer `0x82` DER length encoding, and is sent as separate 1/2/1/97/131-byte TLS application writes, a remaining-body write, then the final 11 authInfo bytes immediately followed in the same client application write by a 9-byte unrelated marker. The production R2 reader must reach `CredentialsVerified` and then the existing genuine native Admission denial while `postTypeTwoPlaintextBytes` equals exactly the combined Type-3/pubKeyAuth TSRequest plus final authInfo size: the 9-byte tail must not be consumed by CredSSP. The same case first repeats the incomplete-final-frame + `close_notify` retirement and ends with a clean same-listener retry using fresh NTLM/TLS connection state. It never creates native R2 admission, MCS, Share, graphics or clipboard authority.

**Size/arithmetic and ownership audit:** `kMaximumCredSspRequestBytes` is 16 KiB while R1's bounded TLS application-I/O cap is 18 KiB. `TsRequestFrameReader` owns one 16 KiB contiguous buffer, computes canonical DER lengths with checked `buffer_.size() - header`, `expected_ - buffered_` and remaining-span arithmetic, and calls R1 with `min(512, bytesNeeded())`. It therefore never asks `SSL_read_ex` for plaintext beyond one TSRequest boundary; a coalesced tail remains in the exact connection-owned SSL. Existing `security.credssp-stream-coalesced` separately exercises manual framing through a 16,000-byte authInfo. Final CredSSP is TLS application DER, not TPKT; TPKT ownership starts only after authenticated/admitted MCS progression.

**R1 contract for Agents 2, 6 and 10:** complete final authInfo delivery means the sole `TsRequestFrameReader` reaches Complete on the exact pinned R1 owner, transport generation, SSL and certificate, R2 synchronously accepts a `finalAuthInfoOnly()` frame, and `releaseFrame()` succeeds. A TLS close-notify, FIN, reset, alert or invalid TLS result before Complete is terminal: the reader closes/wipes its buffered framing state and cannot produce `CredentialsVerified`. Server-binding write completion means `TsRequestTlsReplyWriter` reaches Complete through R1's accepted plaintext writes and `releaseReply()` revalidates the same generation/SSL/certificate; it is **local write completion only, never peer receipt**. Connection retirement closes the R2 writer/reader before R1 cancels SSL/BIO/socket ownership; a replacement accepted connection receives a fresh nonzero R1 transport generation and fresh SSL/BIO/CredSSP frame state.

**Correction parent:** `b93e8110f44558f07c096132977856dd54db97a4`. The immediately preceding R3 publication

is rejected. The focused gate is renamed

SendData, Attach/Join confirms, membership, SendDataIndication, GCC nodeID and
RDPGFX against that Microsoft-profile boundary. No live authentication,
admission, MCS progression or Share activation is fabricated.

## R1 P0 follow-up — zero-timeout readiness dwell attribution (2026-10-29)

**Parent:** `12af8f1e5946250138f222721e91497543e50889`. Current source
inspection found one diagnostic attribution gap, not a transport-wire defect:
the GUI HostControl intentionally checks socket readiness with a zero timeout,
so time spent *inside* `poll()` cannot represent the full interval for which
R1 remains in `NeedRead` or `NeedWrite`. A multi-second peer/readiness wait
could therefore be folded into the old residual bucket.

The same accepted-connection `steady_clock` now accounts wall-clock dwell by
the authoritative R1 Read/Write interest between bounded service calls. Actual
native-poll duration is retained as a non-additive subset, and the existing
poller latches readiness-observed -> next matching service delay without
reading the socket. No second reader, packet clock, TLS parser, timer, timeout

non-Read/Write phases such as explicit TLS configuration/observation gaps and
must not be labeled peer delay.

`0xe08a8235`; eight-byte server nonce; eight zero reserved bytes; TargetInfo

then AV pairs `MsvAvNbDomainName=RDP`, `MsvAvNbComputerName=RDP-SERVER`,
`MsvAvTimestamp=<fresh FILETIME>`, terminal `MsvAvEOL`. The independent
fixture now checks every one of those header fields, offsets, lengths, values,

`0x02000000` removed, plus server-only TARGET_TYPE_SERVER
`0x00020000` and TARGET_INFO `0x00800000` added. UNICODE,
REQUEST_TARGET, SIGN, SEAL, NTLM, ALWAYS_SIGN, EXTENDED_SESSIONSECURITY, 128,

confidentiality and key-exchange properties required by the standalone

Version bytes is standards-compliant and does not affect NTLM processing.

is version 6 and carries exactly one raw Direct-NTLM Type 1 in `negoTokens`;

envelope. The final raw Type 3 is accepted only in the same final negotiation
request with `pubKeyAuth`/nonce; the server binding reply omits
`negoTokens`, and `authInfo` is accepted only after binding succeeds. This
matches the existing MS-CSSP final-token/binding ordering and does not weaken
MIC, sign/seal or credential verification.

uncaptured DomainName/Workstation SECURITY_BUFFER descriptors at bytes 16..31
as explicitly unknown. Their normalized zeros are test input only, not claimed

## Agent 6 P0 — request CredSSP stream semantics for the wire oracle (2026-10-26)

**Reconciled parent:** `08ce14baed353415a11f0926cbceb0c2a3f673ba`. Exact-parent Windows run `40295613485`, job `121480868153`, passes both harness-integrity CTests and both independent Microsoft NTLM Type-2 oracles, then fails the fixed-name full-CREDSSP control before the first TSRequest. The successful Microsoft sequence is 153-byte TLS handshake output -> 1222-byte server TLS flight -> 158-byte TLS handshake output -> 226-byte server TLS flight -> 94-byte output with `SEC_I_CONTINUE_NEEDED`. On the exact parent that 94-byte output classifies as `opaque-other`; OpenSSL consumes zero plaintext and reports `0x0a000139` (record-layer failure). Therefore it is not valid evidence to feed that token into the production TLS BIO as a TLS record.

The harness was requesting `ISC_REQ_CONNECTION` from Microsoft CREDSSP. Microsoft's API contract defines that flag as a context that does **not** handle message formatting, while `ISC_REQ_STREAM` requests a stream-oriented context. Because this oracle directly connects Microsoft's CREDSSP client output to the production OpenSSL wire peer, this increment changes only the test client's context requirement from `ISC_REQ_CONNECTION` to `ISC_REQ_STREAM`, retaining `ISC_REQ_ALLOCATE_MEMORY` and `ISC_REQ_MANUAL_CRED_VALIDATION`. The existing scripted multi-turn harness CTest now explicitly requires stream semantics and rejects connection semantics.

This is a test-harness contract correction, not a production wire/profile change. Production Type-2 flags, TargetName, TargetInfo, MsvAvTargetName, TLS certificate identity, SPNEGO/CredSSP production framing, native Admission, MCS, Share, graphics, input and clipboard remain **UNCHANGED**. The independent inner NTLM oracle remains unchanged.

## P0 NTLM Type-2 compatibility audit; production unchanged pending Windows SSPI oracle (2026-10-25)

**Assignment main:** `1e6a7c6ea11fcfde09061355328080591a6d7e30`.
**Reconciled main parent:** `0ef7a980e0bea8c4ce69bbf3b134e355ce2b45f6`.
Owner physical Linux/X11 evidence is 980/980 CTest PASS and reaches
`TLS -> raw Direct NTLM Type 1 -> server Type 2 fully delivered -> peer EOF`
with no Type 3. Native Admission, MCS and graphics are not reached. The first
unresolved boundary is Microsoft-client acceptance of the Type 2.

The exact observed flag delta is `0xe2088235 -> 0xe08a8235`:

| Flag | Type 1 -> Type 2 | Audit result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UNICODE `0x00000001` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; negotiated Unicode |
| REQUEST_TARGET `0x00000004` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; the challenge supplies the bounded server TargetName |
| SIGN `0x00000010` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; return when offered |
| SEAL `0x00000020` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; return when offered |
| NTLM `0x00000200` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; standalone NTLM profile |
| ALWAYS_SIGN `0x00008000` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; selected consistently across negotiate/challenge |
| TARGET_TYPE_SERVER `0x00020000` | 0 -> 1 | server-selected; legal in CHALLENGE_MESSAGE and bound to the non-empty server TargetName |
| EXTENDED_SESSIONSECURITY `0x00080000` | 1 -> 1 | preserved; required standalone security profile |
| TARGET_INFO `0x00800000` | 0 -> 1 | server-selected; accurately announces populated TargetInfo |
| VERSION `0x02000000` | 1 -> 0 | the only cleared client bit; current production keeps the fixed Version field zero |
| 128 `0x20000000` | 1 -> 1 | preserved with SIGN/SEAL |
| KEY_EXCH `0x40000000` | 1 -> 1 | preserved only because the client offered it |
| 56 `0x80000000` | 1 -> 1 | preserved with SIGN/SEAL |

No other bits differ. MS-NLMP defines VERSION as debugging-only metadata that
does not affect normal NTLM processing, so specification review alone does not
justify enabling it. The production profile therefore stays unchanged until a
Microsoft-native Windows SSPI oracle consumes the exact production Type 2 and
shows that preserving VERSION is required. If later enabled, it must be
client-offered only and use portable version semantics rather than claiming a
Windows release.

Current TargetInfo remains exactly AV IDs `2,1,7,0`: NetBIOS domain,
NetBIOS computer, timestamp and EOL. Do not fabricate DNS computer/domain
values, MsvAvFlags or MsvAvTargetName for this standalone non-domain server.
MsvAvFlags/MIC, MsvAvTargetName and channel-binding checks affect later
AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE semantics and are not added to Type 2 without
Microsoft-native oracle evidence.

Transcript audit: `StandaloneSpnegoNtlmAcceptor::issueChallenge()` copies the
exact received Type 1 bytes into `negotiateMessage_`, encodes Type 2 once into
`challengeMessage_`, sends those same bytes, and later passes the exact stored
spans to `verifyAuthenticateMessageMic()`. No normalized or re-encoded
transcript exists.

Test-only compatibility coverage now has three bounded profiles:
(1) the current production portable profile and exact physical flag delta,
(2) an offered-VERSION-preserved variant whose only differences are the VERSION
bit and fixed Version field and whose zero product version deliberately does
not impersonate Windows, and (3) Microsoft's published MS-NLMP 4.2.4.3
CHALLENGE_MESSAGE. The independent test oracle now understands the fixed
56-byte header and validates negotiated VERSION reserved/revision bytes. These
profiles are not user-selectable and do not alter production.

**SSPI dependency:** current-main reconciliation found no Microsoft-native
Windows SSPI Type-2 oracle result to consume. Production challenge bytes are
therefore **UNCHANGED** and no new Linux physical candidate is nominated.

## R9/R10 P0 — same-port restart after server-active close (2026-10-24)

**Starting exact-main parent:** `0dd28a0a6840eb343b1dae4fa13ec2d9f73ea00c`.

The hosted native-admission correction worked: exact-SHA run
`40129269378`, job `120977311045`, compiled the production-linked
DirectNtlm lifecycle and the valid reconnect peer reached the expected
`CredentialsVerified -> Admission denied` boundary. The R9 gate then failed
later at the first fresh Start after ordinary Stop:
`startSharingOnPort(control, recommendation, selectedPort)`.

This exposes a real R1/R10 lifecycle dependency rather than an authentication
failure. The rejected authenticated peer is actively closed by the server.
On POSIX, the accepted local endpoint can therefore remain in TCP
`TIME_WAIT` after the listener is closed. The exact-address production LAN
listener did not set `SO_REUSEADDR`, so immediate restart on the user's same
configured port could fail with `PortOccupied`. The older three-cycle
Start/Stop fixture used a client-side close and did not exercise this server
active-close case.

The POSIX listener now sets `SO_REUSEADDR` before its exact-address bind.
It deliberately does **not** use `SO_REUSEPORT`; a second concurrently live
listener on the same exact endpoint must still return `PortOccupied`.
Dedicated native regression
`transport.lan-listener-same-port-rebind-after-server-close` makes the server
the active closer, observes EOF at the peer, closes the listener and requires
an immediate same-port rebind with a fresh listener generation while preserving
the live-duplicate denial. The focused R9 sanitizer gate compiles and directly
executes this regression before the full DirectNtlm reconnect/Stop->Start
lifecycle.

No CredSSP, NTLM, native-admission, MCS, graphics or clipboard authority is
changed. If exact-SHA hosted R9 plus Linux/macOS/Windows protocol jobs are green,

**Starting exact-main parent:** `03121aab30c6807d611e0995aded9b0a50e395b2`.

Owner wire evidence still stops inside R1 TLS: TCP/X.224 succeeds, HYBRID is
selected, the server certificate is presented, and the connection closes during
the TLS handshake. There is no demonstrated client CredSSP TSRequest,
`CredentialsVerified`, or MCS traffic. **R3 wire changes therefore remain
BLOCKED.** This increment changes no MCS, Share, licensing or RDPGFX production
wire code.

The real-client classification order is now explicit:

1. **TLS established** — require R1's established TLS diagnostic/transition.
   Merely presenting the certificate, entering `AwaitTls`, or receiving TCP
   bytes is not this boundary.
2. **first CredSSP TSRequest** — require evidence that the owner-bound
   `TsRequestFrameReader` completed the first DER TSRequest from established
   R1 TLS. `LinuxRuntimeCredSspDiagnosticTransition::AwaitingToken` means only
   “TLS established and awaiting CredSSP”; it must not be reported as a received
   TSRequest.
3. **CredentialsVerified** — require the existing
   `LinuxRuntimeCredSspDiagnosticTransition::CredentialsVerified`, which is
   published only after the production authenticated-principal proof binds to
   the same R1 TLS/CredSSP owner.
4. **MCS Connect-Initial** — this becomes R3's first owned failure boundary only
   after `CredentialsVerified`. Before successful intake the R3 phase is
   `AwaitVerifiedR2Admission`; an admitted Connect-Initial advances it to
   `AwaitConnectResponse`.
5. **MCS Connect-Response** — a fully accepted response write advances the R3
   phase from `AwaitConnectResponse` to `AwaitErectDomain`. R1 write
   readiness or partial progress is not response completion.

If a future owner-authorized Microsoft-client trace reaches
`CredentialsVerified` and then fails before `AwaitConnectResponse`, R3 owns
the first bad Connect-Initial transition. If it reaches
`AwaitConnectResponse` and fails before `AwaitErectDomain`, R3 owns the
Connect-Response transition. Until one of those facts exists, do not patch MCS,
Share, licensing or RDPGFX wire behavior.

Stop/reconnect source ownership is also pinned without fabricating a positive
client. `retireStoppedRuntime()` revokes the accepted
`LinuxRuntimeConnection` before clearing it and before closing the R1
listener. `LinuxRuntimeConnection::revoke()` closes first-MCS framing and the
R3 session/lease before cancelling R1. `McsSessionLifecycle::close()` clears
admission/session generations, Connect-Response allocation/writer state,
joins, licensing, Share, clipboard and Graphics lifetimes and ends in
`Closed`. `clearAcceptedClient()` destroys that aggregate and resets the
HostControl accepted-client phase to `None`; a later accept constructs a new
`LinuxRuntimeConnection` with a new value-owned `McsSessionLifecycle` and
fresh reconnect generation.

Dedicated offline source-contract CTest:
`runtime.linux-host-control-stop-retires-protocol-session-state`. It does not open a
listener, create credentials, read a desktop or generate protocol bytes.

**R3 freshness result:** source ownership proves no R3/MCS session state can
survive an ordinary Stop into a later accepted connection. The requested full
product **Start -> Stop -> Start** execution is still **BLOCKED** by the
independent HostControl credential-lifetime defect: current ordinary Stop also
revokes the standalone memory-only credential, so a second Start cannot proceed
without password re-entry. R3 must not “solve” that blocker by retaining MCS
state or changing wire behavior.

Author-side connector/source review: **PASS**. Canonical
`~/rdp-server/build` configure/build/full CTest: **NOT RUN** in this
connector-only environment. Real Microsoft-client post-TLS/CredSSP/MCS
acceptance: **NOT RUN / BLOCKED at R1 TLS**.

**R3 next gate:** wait for R1 evidence of TLS established. Then classify the
first completed CredSSP TSRequest and `CredentialsVerified`; only if the trace
crosses `CredentialsVerified` does R3 take immediate ownership of the first
failing Connect-Initial/Connect-Response transition.

## macOS LAN route selection and GUI form growth updates (2026-10-24)

Starting exact-main parent: `f7876df97d2b280941de51071ab76a4988188351`.

Addressed macOS native runtime host network selection and GUI presentation feedback:
- Resolved ambiguous network selection when virtual bridges or VPN tunnels exist alongside
  the primary physical network interface:
  - Excluded point-to-point interfaces (`IFF_POINTOPOINT`) in `MacRuntimeHostControl::enumerateLocalInterfaces()`,
    ensuring VPN and tunnel endpoints (such as `ipsec*`, `utun*`) are excluded from LAN candidates.
  - Implemented `readMacDefaultRoutePreferences()` querying `SCDynamicStore` for active network
    services with configured default gateways/routers (`State:/Network/Service/.*/IPv4`).
  - Implemented `recommendMacPrivateLanEndpoint()` in `src/server/runtime/mac_runtime_host_control.cpp`,
    marking matching default-route interfaces with `preferredRoute = true` and `routeMetric = 10`,
    and giving physical Ethernet/Wi-Fi (`en*`) interfaces precedence over virtual bridge interfaces.
  - As a result, the primary physical network interface (e.g. `en0` at `192.168.1.6`) is selected
    as the authoritative recommended private LAN endpoint without ambiguity.
- Resolved font height and label truncation in the Advanced tab's Security section:
  - Configured `setFieldGrowthPolicy(QFormLayout::AllNonFixedFieldsGrow)` on `accessForm`,
    `networkForm`, and `securityForm` in `DesktopWindow` (`src/gui/desktop_window.cpp`).
  - On macOS, Qt's native style defaults `fieldGrowthPolicy` to `FieldsStayAtSizeHint`, which
    clamped multi-line status labels to narrow widths and truncated wrapped lines;
    `AllNonFixedFieldsGrow` allows fields to expand across the full column width and
    accurately compute row heights.
- Registered new behavior CTest in `tests/CMakeLists.txt`:
  `runtime.macos-host-control-lan-endpoint-recommendation`.

Verification: 744/744 tests **PASS** on macOS Debug.

## R3 P0 automatic portable licensing identity — 2026-10-23

Starting exact-main parent: `f184a077300c8b4fa46384891835cbf3a550a4b8`.

Normal no-argument GUI startup no longer needs external RDP licensing
certificate/private-key/ProductInfo fields. R3 adds
`RuntimeLicensingContext::configureGeneratedApplicationIdentity()`: fixed
application ProductInfo/scope (`RDP-server`, `RDP-server Personal Desktop`)
is paired with fresh provider-backed RSA-2048 cryptographic material and a
root-first two-certificate X.509 `CERT_CHAIN_VERSION_2`
`SERVER_CERTIFICATE` object. The generated leaf private key exists only in
process memory, is copied into the existing cleansing R3 credential owner, and
is never written to the ZIP, a file, argv, environment, logs or GUI state.
Expert explicit licensing configuration remains supported.

R1 TLS is **not reused** for licensing. R1's automatic identity is one
endpoint-bound self-signed TLS leaf inside its SSL context; MS-RDPBCGR licensing
requires a distinct `SERVER_CERTIFICATE` chain used by the MS-RDPELE RSA key
exchange. The existing R3 credential validator independently parses the
root-first chain, verifies the root->leaf signature and requires the leaf's
matching RSA private key. Keeping those roles separate also avoids exporting
R1's private TLS key.

directs the owner to an exact Advanced interface choice. Manual override remains
available. Existing fresh Start re-enumeration, stable native-ID resolution,
private-LAN validation, TLS identity binding, R2 authorization and R1 listener

## R6 P1 cross-platform preferred-LAN recommendation contract (2026-10-22)

Starting exact-main parent: `33676c5e0ffc5b831ecbf393ee89174342d245ce`.

R6 reviewed R10's preferred-LAN helper after R1 landed the independent
recommendation-to-bind authority fence. The existing shared helper preferred
IPv4 and then used lexicographic stable-interface/address ordering, which could
accidentally make Linux-shaped identities such as `eth0#...` or
`wlan0#...` part of portable selection policy.

The shared runtime contract now defines platform recommendation facts
semantically: opaque stable interface identity, address, explicit IPv4/IPv6
family, private-LAN eligibility, preferred/default-route ownership, optional
route metric/priority, and an explicit ambiguity result. Preferred-route
ownership outranks non-preferred routes; a lower metric ranks routes only when
every remaining contender has a metric. Equal or incomparable distinct
endpoints are reported ambiguous rather than being broken by interface name,
address text or address family. The current interface-only compatibility path
supplies no invented route facts, so multiple distinct endpoints remain
ambiguous until R10's platform collector supplies them.

`runtime.host-control-cross-platform-lan-recommendation-contract`. It is
platform-neutral/offline and proves a Windows-style opaque identity can carry
the same semantic facts as Linux, IPv4 and IPv6 are explicit, route
ownership/metric drive selection, missing metrics are conservative, and
`eth0`/`wlan0` ordering never resolves a tie. R1's
`runtime.r1-bind-revalidates-recommended-endpoint` remains unchanged and
continues to prove recommendation metadata is not bind authority.

This is recommendation/presentation policy only. It opens no socket, starts no
listener, reads no native routing API, grants no R2 authority, and does not
change `kWindowsNativeDesktopPositiveActivationApproved` or any Windows
native-host activation path. CLEAN Windows remains a separate R9 acceptance

## R5 macOS row-size compile correction after R10 composition (2026-10-21)

Current parent: `419e5d8ab0f81e7d717170bcd67c9b98a6799a03`.

`protocol (macos-latest)` job `119653293665` and
`r7-macos-native-lifecycle` job `119653293822`: Clang rejects the

64-bit `size_t::max()/4` as a tautological out-of-range comparison under

multiply bound and reuse that cached value for tight BGRA row bytes. This
preserves the existing overflow/fail-closed behavior without weakening the
512 MiB mailbox cap or changing capture/input authority. The dedicated
`macos.native-desktop-owner-framebuffer-row-size-bounds` CTest prevents the
cross-width comparison from returning.

blockers. After this correction, remaining R5 gates are exact-publication-SHA
macOS build/CTest qualification and explicit owner authorization for live TCC,
ScreenCaptureKit, visible desktop and Quartz input execution. Linux FIRST
remains frozen at `8f2667b9d4a9dd09b05486e91c3277fc3cb4af72` and is not
requalified by this change.

## R5 macOS authorized native desktop aggregate (2026-10-21)

Starting shared-main parent: `6b99b2abdd599cc3e8d249b013927050ee8dd78f`.

R2 Track E landed while this work was in progress, so R5 now consumes the real
`MacNativeDesktopAuthorization` rather than leaving a placeholder seam. The
new Apple-only `MacNativeDesktopOwner` is the single native desktop lifetime
R10 may own. Positive construction, bounded service, framebuffer borrow and
input dispatch all execute inside the exact expected R2 authorization-generation
visitor; UID, display ID, geometry/session generations, TCC state and owner
consent scalars cannot construct or operate the owner by themselves.

The aggregate owns one process-scoped display reconfiguration watch, one native
GUI-session change watch, one admitted R2 generation, one validated display
geometry generation, one `MacDesktopSessionGuard`, one one-shot
ScreenCaptureKit stream, and at most one Quartz input controller. View-only R2
authorization constructs capture without an input route. View+Input additionally
requires fresh Accessibility trust and Input Monitoring readiness before
construction and again at each input operation. Screen Recording readiness is
checked before capture construction and
on every service/borrow lifetime check through the existing guard.

ScreenCaptureKit's private serial callback never enters R2 or protocol state.
It copies only the newest complete BGRA frame into one reusable bounded mailbox,
stripping native row padding. R10 receives synchronous service/borrow/revoke
operations; there is no worker/server/protocol loop. A borrow names the exact
latest frame sequence and runs under a fresh R2 View visit. The current native
composition intentionally refuses multi-display virtual layouts because one
ScreenCaptureKit stream publishes one display while input uses virtual-desktop
coordinates; this fails closed until a compositor/multi-stream policy is owned.

Display changes, lock/logout/user/session replacement, TCC loss, capture
failure, geometry/session fence loss, or R2 authorization replacement retire
the aggregate terminally. Authority-loss teardown calls
`retireWithoutNativeInput()` before native children disappear, so held
modifiers/buttons are discarded rather than released into a replacement
desktop. Fresh authorization and a fresh aggregate are required to reconnect.

The production ScreenCaptureKit backend and Quartz posting callbacks remain
private friend-only seams of `MacNativeDesktopOwner`; no UID/display-only or
TCC-only constructor was added. Dedicated ordinary Apple CTests are
`macos.native-desktop-owner-fail-closed-construction`,
`macos.native-desktop-owner-frame-input-lifecycle`, and
`macos.native-desktop-owner-display-session-retirement`. They use the real
R2 authorization state machine with synthetic native evidence and injected
macOS side-effect seams; they never enumerate a live display, request TCC,
start ScreenCaptureKit or post Quartz events.

Canonical owner-local configure/build/full CTest: **NOT RUN** in this connector
environment. Exact-publication-SHA hosted macOS CI: **PENDING**. Live Screen
Recording, Accessibility/Quartz input, listener and remote-client operation:
**NOT RUN**.

Linux FIRST remains separate and frozen at `8f2667b9…`; this macOS composition
does not move or requalify that SHA. Its owner-authorized physical sequence
(native desktop ready -> framebuffer -> visible desktop -> mouse -> clicks ->
keyboard -> modifier retirement -> Stop -> reconnect -> one resize) remains

## R2 NTLMSSP fixed Version-field correction (2026-10-20)

Follow-up to `2131703acd28db77f6a6951139f18cc45fed7e01`: re-reading the
published MS-NLMP structures found that NEGOTIATE_MESSAGE, CHALLENGE_MESSAGE
and AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE retain their 8-byte Version field even when
NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_VERSION is clear; the field is then all zero. The first
framing commit incorrectly treated that field as absent when the flag was
clear, moving the server TargetInfo eight bytes early and allowing too-low
payload floors in the no-Version parser case.

The corrected wire owner uses fixed 40/56/72-byte Type 1/2/3 headers, requires
the Type 1/3 Version bytes to be zero when the flag is clear, keeps the server
Type 2 Version bytes zero, and starts a required Type 3 MIC only after the fixed
72-byte header. The dedicated challenge oracle and MIC-alias denial fixture are
updated with those exact offsets. This is a source-level correction only; no
new capability or interoperability claim is added.

Owner-local build/full CTest: **NOT RUN** in this connector environment.
Exact publication-SHA hosted CI: **PENDING**.

## R2 M1 positive local-owner authority (2026-10-19)

M1 now trusts the currently logged-in local desktop-user session plus explicit
interaction with the locally running server GUI as the local consent boundary.
It does not claim resistance to malicious processes already running as the
same UID or to X11 clients capable of synthetic input; same-user/X11 compromise
is explicitly outside the M1 threat model.

R10 owns one noncopyable CurrentOwnerSharingAuthority. A positive grant requires
fresh native process UID, active physical non-remote seat0, exact session ID and
start generation/display, known-unlocked login1 LockedHint, requested scope and
a short lifetime (hard maximum one hour). Accepted connections receive only a
const authority borrow, so no network peer can grant consent. Every protected

## R2 Linux/X11 trusted-owner blocker and offline NLA feasibility (2026-10-19)

R10's concrete Linux `LinuxRuntimeHostControl` is already on `main`; R2 is
not waiting for an R10 interface. The specifically supported X11 environment
investigated is **Ubuntu Desktop 24.04 LTS / GNOME 46 / Ubuntu on Xorg /
physical local non-root seat0 user session**, with native UID, session ID,
session-start generation and X11 display read from logind.

**Positive-owner decision: BLOCKED for the no-install portable ZIP.** The
precise missing capability is a secure-attention / physical-origin approval
channel that an untrusted X11 client cannot synthesize. Xorg XTEST deliberately
allows clients to inject key, button and pointer events, so a portal/polkit/GTK
approval dialog in the same X11 session cannot by itself prove a physical-owner
action. GNOME `org.gnome.ScreenSaver` can add lock-state observation but does
not supply that secure-attention guarantee. Consequently no portable native
composition on this target provides all required facts in one verifiable trust
chain: affirmative physical-owner approval, exact OS/session/seat binding,
authoritative unlocked state, exact view/input/clipboard scope plus deadline,
and mandatory revocation on lock/logout/user switch/session replacement/native
authority loss. logind is
retained for session identity/lifecycle but its `LockedHint` is
desktop-supplied; XDG RemoteDesktop provides a native consent/device-scope
interaction but does not contractually bind that grant to the exact logind
session or require lock-triggered closure; polkit user authentication neither
attests desktop unlock nor preserves ZIP-only deployment for an
application-specific installed action. Qt/X11 intent is not trusted evidence.

**Superseded current-state correction (2026-10-21):** this deny-only directive no longer describes M1. `CurrentOwnerSharingAuthority::requestConsent()` accepts fresh valid physical seat0/unlocked same-UID evidence, issues a bounded grant, and `authorizes()` freshly revalidates it. Lock/unknown, expiry, logout, user switch, session replacement and native-authority loss still revoke. Offline positive fixtures are not physical FIRST evidence.

**R10 handoff once a qualifying provider exists:** R2 alone creates one opaque
move-only/noncopyable `OwnerSharingLease` bound to exact native owner
identity, granted permission mask, monotonic deadline, R2 generation and
native-provider generation. Consent must be asynchronous so native human
interaction never blocks the Qt/R10 owner thread. R2 re-reads the complete
native binding after positive interaction before lease issuance. R10 owns the
lease and freshly reauthorizes before Start/listener bind, after potentially
blocking bind/native work, before client admission, and at every existing R3
View/R5 Input/R8 Clipboard protected transition. Hot-path authorization is
cached/bounded; native event watchers revoke off the hot path. Stop,
lock/unknown, logout, switch, session replacement, credential-policy change,
expiry or provider loss invalidates R2 first, retires R3/native/client state,
then closes R1.

**Independent application password:** current production remains unsupported.
CredSSP establishes SPNEGO before encrypted final `TSPasswordCreds`; the
current GSS acceptor is Kerberos-only, so PAM or an application password hash
cannot by themselves authenticate unmodified Microsoft clients. A reviewed
domainless **NTLMv2-over-SPNEGO** provider is protocol-feasible in principle:
MS-NLMP supports local NT one-way-function validation and the ISC-licensed
`gssapi/gss-ntlmssp` mechanism supports local NT-hash credentials. The NT
hash is password-equivalent secret material. This candidate still requires
production integration, pinned bundled mechanism/config, secure secret
storage/rotation, CredSSP TLS/public-key binding proof and real offline client
interoperability.

Until then keep **Set Application Password — Unsupported** disabled, never
change the OS password and never downgrade NLA. The exact current OS-account
fallback is a configured/reachable Kerberos realm/KDC, explicit
`TERMSRV/<host>@REALM` acceptor keytab and principal-to-local-account R2
mapping, followed by final PAM password/account verification. A stock local
Linux username/password without Kerberos does not meet the current SPNEGO gate
and therefore does not satisfy the isolated-ZIP product requirement.

**Production-backed evidence:** exact SHA
`c1ec383576c52629a2f094ed8a696d2280720b8c` has primary Actions
`39207508411` **PASS** and structure Actions `39207508301` **PASS**,
including `r2-linux-production-runtime-security (complete)`,
`r2-linux-production-runtime-security (missing-systemd)`,
`r9-security-protocol-sanitizers` and Ubuntu/macOS/Windows protocol jobs.
This is negative/session-consistency evidence, not positive physical consent.

Required future state-machine tests: exact native-binding match/mismatch around
consent completion; move-only scope/deadline; Stop, lock/unknown, logout,
switch, replacement, credential generation, expiry and provider-loss
revocation; no unlock revival; fresh Start/protected-operation checks; and
R2-before-R3/native-before-R1 teardown. Standalone-password acceptance requires
isolated-LAN `mstsc.exe` and macOS Windows App tests for correct/wrong
credentials, rotation, restart, Unicode, replay/timestamp, TLS identity
rotation, NTLMv1 denial, no DC/KDC/cloud dependency and no NLA downgrade.

No live desktop, credential, listener, service, lock/switch or Microsoft-client
test was authorized or run by this review: **NOT RUN**. Source/document review:

## R2 canonical peer quota across dual-stack address encodings (2026-10-18)

R2's serialized NLA attempt limiter now treats native IPv4 and exact
`::ffff:a.b.c.d` IPv4-mapped IPv6 as the **same** fixed-table peer.

distinct active slots and increase the attempts allowed per peer on a
future authorized dual-stack LAN listener. Only the RFC 4291
ten-zero/two-0xff prefix canonicalizes; native and near-mapped IPv6
remain distinct. The update is zero allocation and changes neither
global nor per-GSS-principal budgets or the current deny-only LAN
host-control admission.

# RDP-server roadmap — authoritative live status

**Reconciled:** 2026-10-17 · **Shared branch:** `main` · **Milestones accepted:** 0/6  
**Baseline inspected before this coordination update:** `8f3c2f06b305eca60708867c9e50f9a6a59a79cb`.  
**Decision:** **M1 OPEN / NOT ACCEPTED.** Hosted tests alone cannot satisfy owner-native acceptance.  
**Status vocabulary:** DONE = component delivered with specified evidence; READY = implementation ready for its next integration; BLOCKED = external/dependency gate; ACTIVE = one bounded increment in progress; NOT RUN = missing evidence.

This file is the **only active roadmap and cross-agent communication board**. It replaces the former chronological append-only progress diary. Earlier details are recoverable in Git history; exact test/CI evidence and historical failure diagnostics reside in `docs/CODEX_VALIDATION.md`. Do not add per-agent progress documents, repeat old reports, or append a dated section for each commit.

## R2 P0 standalone Microsoft CredSSP credential decision (2026-10-18)

**Decision: A, existing OS-backed accounts for first Linux/X11 acceptance; B, an independent GUI-password verifier, is BLOCKED.** This is a feasibility decision, not a claim that the complete product works. Neither `Configure password` nor `Start Sharing` may create an R2 lease or activate a LAN listener/Share. The new production `security/standalone_credential_policy.h` exposes a deny-only GUI credential-choice assessment, and `security.lan-credential-mode-denials` CTest verifies OS-account selection, unconfigured/unknown modes and independent-password refusal. Its `mayStartSharingFromCredentialChoice` predicate is always false: actual admission continues exclusively through the private R2 native broker. Do not use this predicate as a replacement for that broker.

**Mechanism feasibility and non-goals.** Microsoft MS-CSSP uses TLS, SPNEGO with Kerberos or NTLM, TLS public-key binding and delegated credentials; a salted application password hash alone cannot answer an NTLMv2 challenge nor provide Kerberos tickets. Kerberos requires an independently accessible KDC/ticket/service key; an offline LAN with no configured realm does not have that infrastructure. Windows SSPI offers Kerberos/NTLM/Negotiate; Linux MIT/Heimdal GSS offer Kerberos and optional `gss-ntlmssp`/Samba integration; macOS GSS supports Kerberos, but an equivalent first-party NTLM server acceptor and client negotiation cannot be assumed. `gss-ntlmssp` can use a password file or winbind credentials, but this introduces plaintext/NTLM-equivalent reusable verifier material and a mechanism-specific security audit. Windows clients may reject NTLM under policy (including NTLM block policies); Windows App behavior on Windows/macOS is not verified. Do not fall back to TLS-only RDP, change client policies, claim a generic SPNEGO application-password OID is supported, or implement a proprietary login exchange. Sources: MS-CSSP, Microsoft Credential Security Support Provider/NTLM policy, gssapi/gss-ntlmssp.

**Executable feasibility ladder, with pass criteria per client.** (1) Linux opt-in isolated machine with physical logged-in X11 `seat0` owner: configure the already-existing explicit `TERMSRV/host@REALM` keytab, corresponding account-to-UID mapping and dedicated PAM service (not an unreviewed GUI password store); retain no GUI copy of delegated credentials. Offline means no internet, not necessarily no LAN KDC; verify KDC availability, otherwise mark Kerberos **BLOCKED**. (2) Run an isolated NTLMv2 acceptor spike **without** desktop/Share, using approved real credential backend, inspect GSS flags, binding/replay/session-security properties and secure verifier storage; any dependency on plaintext/NT hash requires security design review, not promotion. (3) For each Windows 11 `mstsc.exe`, Windows App Windows, Windows App macOS, record actual version/build, client policy, X.224 HYBRID, TLS certificate and first-use trust, SPNEGO selected OID, MIC/channel/public-key binding, delegated identity, failure code and packet trace ID; test Kerberos and NTLM distinctly, reject fallback. All client outcomes **NOT RUN**. (4) Only after actual complete credentials and fresh logind/NSS physical-owner consent may the existing broker mint its nonfabricable lease, then R10/R3 admit Share.

**GUI lifecycle contract.** OS-account mode selects an existing real account, never changes the OS password, uses the client's own standard credential prompt and platform keychain only if explicitly requested by the client. Configure/replace/revoke access updates an R2 policy generation; revocation retires every old lease, pending handshake and R3/desktop/input capability before renewed use. Explicit host-user consent must be per live owner session and bound to UID, seat/session ID, logind generation, unlocked/active status, and approved view/control permissions; owner logout/switch/lock, password/account disabling, policy replacement, or TLS listener identity change causes termination and fresh consent. A configured OS account does not prove physical ownership. Require bounded failed-attempt throttling per peer **and** account with global overload protection (avoid account-enumeration and memory exhaustion); maintain fixed-size/expired attempt slots and generic wire denials. Audit only status/trace, never passwords, hashes, NT responses, authInfo, tickets or bearer capabilities. GUI distinctions: `CREDENTIAL_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `UNSUPPORTED_APPLICATION_PASSWORD_NLA`, `OS_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `OS_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`, `HOST_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, `HOST_SESSION_STALE`, `ACCESS_REVOKED`, `AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, `TLS_IDENTITY_UNTRUSTED`; external authentication failures must not disclose account existence. After termination, reauthorization reruns the whole OS and transport evidence chain. Offline account verification needs an actually available OS/PAM provider and compatible Kerberos/NTLM mechanism; availability is not implied by ZIP extraction.

**TLS identity UX.** R1 owns certificate generation/persistence and configured LAN interface binding. Before client connection, GUI must show hostname/IP, certificate SHA-256 fingerprint, validity window, persistence/rotation status and whether a trusted chain exists. On first use, the native Microsoft client must show its genuine certificate warning/trust path; never auto-accept, bypass pinning or promise that all clients support in-app TOFU. Certificate rotation requires fresh user confirmation and invalidates relevant policy/transport generations.

**Future providers (not first release).** Windows: native SSPI acceptor + authenticated token SID, WTS session ID, active console owner and secure desktop/lock state, explicit user consent, logon-session revocation and ACL-backed policy, without confusing SID lookup with authenticated login. macOS: genuinely authenticated local UID, audited authorization/login provider plus console session owner, ScreenCaptureKit/TCC permissions, lock/switch revocation and keychain; do not infer authentication from username or GUI checkbox. Both require independent native R2 admission implementations and real clients. Test matrix: incorrect password, nonexistent account, no owner consent, locked/switched/stale session, replay/changed TLS identity, permission loss, revocation after Share and late input; every failure must prevent a visible frame and input. **No positive native-client result is claimed.**

**Current evidence:** source/CTest authored; local Debug build/CTest **NOT RUN** (no approved local checkout); exact publication-SHA hosted CI **PENDING**, live Windows/macOS clients **NOT RUN**. **Next gate:** R2/R10 integrate a truly authenticated OS provider and host-owner consent into start/stop + R3, then record three independent client results. ## M2 integration order and authorization contracts

1. **R1 → R2:** one established HYBRID TLS owner, exact certificate/protocol context and GSS principal, final protected CredSSP `authInfo`; R2 verifies the authenticated account against fresh native interactive-console evidence and alone mints the revocable admission lifetime.
2. **R2 → R3:** active lease, exact user/session/policy generations and monitored revocation allow protected MCS/licensing/Share transitions. Logout, session replacement or owner mismatch is terminal; principal strings, UID/SID values and success Booleans never authorize.
3. **R10 product policy:** service composition selects exactly one immutable mode. `AppServerIssuerBacked` keeps the existing `RuntimeLicensingAuthority::NoVerifiedIssuer` fail-closed path unless a supported provider is separately configured. `PersonalDesktop` is a distinct MS-RDPELE personal-terminal-server mode: no CAL validation/issuance is requested, at most one interactive console session is claimed per connection, and native-session revocation remains mandatory. Policy selection alone grants no R2/R3/native authority.
4. **R2 → R3 personal path:** with the same genuine lease and exact R1 owner freshly reauthorized, R2 consumes R10's `PersonalDesktop` policy and alone invokes R3's private selector before Server License Request. R3 then owns the already-published Valid Client and Share state: after a structurally valid client licensing response it emits `STATUS_VALID_CLIENT` / `ST_NO_TRANSITION`, does not validate a presented CAL, and reaches `ShareActivated` only after exact accepted-byte and client-activation ordering.
5. **R3 application publication:** only current R2 admission plus exact completed R3 personal licensing/activation may expose DRDYNVC/Graphics/input/clipboard routes. App-server mode continues to require genuine issuer-backed licensing instead; neither mode can use a test provider or a policy object as desktop authority.
6. **R10 controlled listener seam:** personal mode may explicitly enable only an exact loopback transport candidate (127.0.0.1 or ::1) and a nonzero port. This policy opens no socket and accepts no client. A real bounded listener remains gated on published non-forgeable R2 admission and R3 activated-session capabilities and explicit owner authorization; no public bind, firewall change or live desktop action is implied.
7. **R4/R5/R6/R7/R8:** consume only current R2 admission + R3 activated session authority. Native generation replacement revokes old capture/input/output; no stale frame/input/file association crosses revocation.

**R7 macOS private R2/R10 authority contract (2026-10-17):** R2 is the only
component allowed to turn authenticated-user proof into native desktop
admission. Its macOS path must authenticate the local account through the
selected real credential mechanism, resolve the immutable local UID, then
compare it with a fresh `MacNativeSessionEvidence` observation:
`consoleUserId == authenticatedUserId == auditUserId == geteuid()`, nonzero
audit session ID, nonzero Security session ID, `sessionHasGraphicAccess`, and
neither `sessionIsRemote` nor `sessionIsRoot`. That observation is evidence,
not the capability. The private R2 lifetime must also carry exact
admission/session generations and revoke on credential/session loss or any
fresh evidence mismatch. No caller UID, Boolean, generation, AppKit/CGSession
fact or TCC status can recreate it.

R10 may compose R7 only while that current R2 lifetime and the same connection's
R3 PersonalDesktop `ShareActivated` authority are both current. R10 is the
sole serializer for `NativeSessionChangeWatch::startNative()/stop()` on a
running AppKit main loop. It derives the R7 target UID only from R2, refreshes
native geometry, owns the revocation-only `MacDesktopSessionGuard`, and checks
Screen Recording or Accessibility only as the operation-specific final OS
prerequisite. The native ScreenCaptureKit backend and Quartz posting callback
remain private/unexposed until this composition exists.

Reauthorize immediately before capture prepare/start, before accepting a
prepared R4 frame for later R3 publication, and immediately before every Quartz
command batch. R2 or R3 loss is terminal even if geometry/session/TCC still
look current: R10 first closes the authority gate, calls
`MacInputController::retireWithoutNativeInput()`, closes the one-shot capture
owner, treats late callbacks as non-publishable, cancels an exact prepared but
unpublished R4 owner when R7 returns `RetireStream`, and retires the AppKit
watch only after R7 owners are terminal. A native event already accepted when
revocation races its callback cannot be retracted, but the outer input
operation must fail and no later release or input event may be posted. Fresh
access requires a new R2 lifetime, fresh R3 Share authority and fresh R7
geometry/session binding.

Enabling it requires Linux GSSAPI/Kerberos, PAM and libsystemd at configure time; missing dependencies fail closed. Dedicated `runtime.linux-security-personal-desktop-preflight-denials` covers unconfigured, wrong-mode and non-admitted native evidence without fabricating seat0 or a lease. **R10 app-server provider feasibility decision (2026-10-17; app-server mode only):** **BLOCKED — project-owner direction required for app-server deployments.** Microsoft [MS-RDPELE] specifies the *client ↔ terminal-server* license PDUs, not the separate *Session Host ↔ license-server* RPC. The architecture describes that RPC for new/upgrade CAL issuance, but this investigation has not identified a documented, supported, authenticated API contract that lets this independent C++23 app-server validate presented CALs and issue/upgrade licenses through Microsoft RD Licensing as an authorized non-Windows Session Host. Windows RD Licensing WMI/PowerShell management/reporting interfaces do not establish such an issuance/verification API. Accordingly **no provider is chosen** for `AppServerIssuerBacked`; that production authority stays `NoVerifiedIssuer`, with no issuer-backed positive completion. The separately approved `PersonalDesktop` mode follows MS-RDPELE personal-terminal-server semantics and does not treat itself as an issuer/provider fallback. The owner must either (a) provide vendor-confirmed interoperability/support terms and an authenticated issuer API for independent app-server use, or (b) explicitly approve a product-scope/licensing-design change before implementing a different compliant provider.

**Required provider contract if supported:** mutual authentication to a specifically pinned issuer identity (Windows/domain credential or service identity and protected transport as documented by its vendor), immutable trust roots/policy and per-request provider-generation binding; explicit signature-chain issuer verification, exact `PRODUCT_INFO` version/company/product ID plus scope, permanent/temporary/upgrade status, expiry including the seven-day upgrade threshold, MAC-verified 20-byte HWID and device/user CAL mode. The R10 authority must bind the provider's verified decision to the 32-byte R3 correlation, digest, positive verification timestamp and live R2 admission/session generations. The owner must supply an activated Windows RD Licensing role, installed and appropriately scoped CAL key packs, supported access credentials and licensing mode, reachable network/domain or workgroup infrastructure, and permission/confirmation from Microsoft or the provider for this app-server integration. An activated licensing server by itself is not a verified R10 backend. MS-RDPELE 1.3.1/3.1.5.1 and Microsoft RD Licensing activation/session-host guidance are the normative references. **External blocker:** supported non-Windows Session Host issuance + existing-CAL validation authority interface and authorization to use it.

**M1 evidence reconciliation:** Repository receipts currently enumerate hosted Actions, not a complete single-SHA set of owner-local Linux/X11, Windows MSYS2 CLANG64/Clang 23 and macOS 27 configure/build/CTest records. Informal owner-reported passes may be valid but cannot establish exact-SHA acceptance without SHA, effective OS/toolchain, configure/build outcomes, complete CTest totals and failed/skipped/not-run counts. **M1 remains OPEN, not a reason to halt unrelated M2 implementation**; request only missing receipt fields, not unnecessary reruns.

**Current personal-desktop M2 dependencies:** R2 must publish protected wrappers that consume R10's immutable `PersonalDesktop` policy only with a genuine live admission lease and exact R1 owner, then invoke R3's private personal selector/Valid Client/Share transitions. Linux real Kerberos/PAM/logind admission remains owner-environment dependent; Windows/macOS still need genuine R2 authenticated native-admission leases. The app-server issuer blocker remains applicable only to `AppServerIssuerBacked`. No synthetic authority or public listener is permitted.

## Shared-main Git coordination contract

- **All agents work directly on the existing `main`** with the canonical checkout/build root. No branches, PRs, worktrees, detached work, patches, force pushes or destructive resets. Git commits, this roadmap and the existing validation ledger are the only cross-agent handoffs; do not rely on chat reports as shared state.
- **Parallel work means independent ownership, not blind parallel writes.** Reserve the active increment's production files to its road. Cross-road integration requires the receiving owner to record the exact consumed API, lifecycle, generation and test in the relevant existing board row before writing. R1 owns TLS, R2 authorization, R3 protocol and wire writers, R4 codec, R5–R7 native owners, R8 clipboard, R9 CI assurance, R10 service/licensing composition.
- **Shared hot spots:** `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/CODEX_VALIDATION.md`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and composition interfaces are collision-sensitive. Each implementation still publishes its own required code + dedicated registered CTest + concise edited roadmap row **atomically in one direct-main commit**. On a conflicting publication, refresh, reconcile both changes, rerun affected checks, then retry without overwrite. R9 coordinates CI selector edits; R10 coordinates only cross-road interface commitments/M1 acceptance, not every unrelated publication.
- **Optimistic publication:** start from a clean fast-forwarded `main`; fetch remote immediately before publishing; ensure the intended commit is based on that current head and changes do not overwrite other agents' updates. If HEAD moved, integrate current upstream changes first; never force, reset, drop another road's work or blindly restore an older complete file. Announce changes **through Git** by updating this board's existing row and citing the new commit/verification.
- **Status edit format:** road, status, exact committed source SHA, tests/CI PASS/FAIL/NOT RUN, blocker, next owner/dependency. Keep one compact row; place only genuinely new acceptance evidence in the existing M1/M2 sections. CI evidence belongs in the one validation ledger as a terse exact-SHA receipt, not mirrored paragraphs throughout the roadmap. Never write a predicted self-SHA into the same commit.
- **M1 publication freeze:** after R10 posts one nominated green candidate, all roads continue **parallel read-only review, local preflight, reproduction planning and dependency analysis**, but do not publish unrelated updates until the owner matrix is complete. Release an urgent real fix only with R10's explicit candidate reset and a fresh hosted + three-owner SHA convergence. Resume atomic independent publication after M1.
- **No work duplication:** inspect current `main` and CTest registrations first. If the behavior already exists and is green, report READY/blocked dependency; do not create a second seam/test/receipt commit. Every new production behavior requires one centrally registered behavior-named production-backed CTest with denial, cancellation/replay and sanitizer coverage where relevant.
- **Pruning:** delete dead code only after checking live call sites, compile variants, tests and consumers; preserve meaningful failure/security tests. Remove obsolete documentation/append-only history after consolidating its current invariant and evidence pointer; Git history is the archive. No broad code cleanup or unrelated CI rewrites during M1. R9 checks test/CI implications and the owning road performs the minimal deletion after freeze.

### R5 decoded wheel to existing native X11 scroll (2026-10-18)

MS-RDPBCGR TS_POINTER_EVENT carries signed 9-bit wheel units
(0x078=+120, 0x188=-120), gives vertical precedence when both
WHEEL/HWHEEL bits are present, and ignores other wheel pointer
flags and untrusted client x/y wheel positions. R5's stateless
R3-decoded translator now produces X11ScrollInput for its already
bounded 120-unit accumulator and XTEST button 4/5 or 6/7 owner,
using zero placeholder coordinates. XTEST uses rootX/Y for motion
only, not button events, so wheel input does not reposition the
pointer. It still requires a valid native geometry. R3 owns
negotiated horizontal-wheel gating; R2 reauthorizes every event
before R5 can reach XTEST. No parallel native owner/TLS reader is
added.

Dedicated offline CTest:
`x11.input-rdp-wheel-sign-extension-axis-and-coordinate-denials`
covers ±120, zero, signed extrema, both axes, precedence,
ignored flags/out-of-range wheel x/y, and malformed non-wheel
and zero-geometry denials. The prior base mapping test now
accepts normative WHEEL/HWHEEL. R10 still disconnects after one
bounded native poll; its persistent R1 TLS post-Share packet
router and first authenticated XShm→R4→R3 frame remain BLOCKED.
Owner full Debug/CTest **NOT RUN**; exact commit hosted CI
**PENDING**; physical seat0/client result **BLOCKED / NOT RUN**
pending explicit owner permission. R9 must separately enroll
the new test in its fixed sanitizer inventory.

### R5 R2-gated native slow-path input bridge (2026-10-18)

R2's `LinuxRuntimeConnection::dispatchPersonalDesktopSlowPathInputPdu`
gateway is now published, so R5 supplies a caller-ready native sink through
`X11AuthorizedInputRoute::dispatchAuthenticatedSlowPathTpkt`. The private
sink can be reached only by the existing R2/R3 per-event authorization.
It holds no copied lease, native descriptor, session cache or second X11
owner. R5 compares the same capture generation before each native event and
retires no-post on any mismatch. An exact, bounded translator handles
ordinary pointer movement, a single left/right/middle button and lock-state
synchronization. It rejects unsupported scancode/unicode/relative/extended/
wheel formats rather than guessing native keyboard layout or using wheel
coordinates the protocol says to ignore. An `Unused` input event is a
gated no-op, not a native request.

`x11.input-r2-authorized-slow-path-native-mapping-denials` is the new
offline CTest for the production translator and the statically-typed R2
gateway interface. No R10 persistent post-Share read loop exists yet,
so input publication is still disabled. R9 and R10 must not advertise
working remote input based on this bridge or synthetic Xvfb.
